sections.h2: Where Genesee County deeds are kept
sections.html:
The County Clerk and Register of Deeds keeps them, in the Genesee County Administration Building at 324 S Saginaw St, Suite 1A, Flint, MI 48502. The office is open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00, with holiday closings.

One elected office oversees vital records, elections and the register of deeds. The register's collection covers deeds, mortgages, liens and other papers touching Genesee land. Recording a paper makes it public. It does not make it legal. Staff index each filing into a searchable database and preserve it, so a flawed deed stays flawed after it is on file.

The statewide default under MCL 600.2567 is a flat $30 per recorded document, whatever its length. Charter counties can pass their own schedule, so get the current sheet from the office before you mail payment.

Recording and copy charges under the state schedule
ServiceCharge
Record one document$30
Extra instruments covered by one discharge or assignment$3 apiece
Photocopies$1 per page
Certification of a recorded paper$5
Index search by request$0.50 per year, $5 floor
Other filings$1

The $30 already includes the state remonumentation share, and $5 of each recording goes to the register's automation fund.

When you mail a deed, enclose a check for the recording fee, any extra instrument charges and any certification you want. Add a note with a phone number so staff can reach you if a paper is incomplete. A document that omits its value, or the affidavit that stands in for it, is the most common reason a closing has to wait.

Fees are due at drop-off. If the register takes electronic filings and you pay electronically, the statute gives one business day after receipt. Ask whether Genesee takes e-filing before you plan a closing around it.

sections.h2: Transfer tax when a deed is recorded
sections.html:
A sale deed brings two levies, and the seller owes both. Michigan's rate is $3.75 per $500 of price, rounded up by $500 block, and the county adds 55 cents on each block because its population is under two million.

The deed must carry the total value in its text, or a value affidavit goes with it. When land and personal property sell together with separate stated values, only the land is taxed. Remit to the county treasurer within 15 days of handing over the deed.

  • Tiny deals: instruments under $100.
  • Loan paper: mortgages and other collateral documents, with their assignments and discharges.
  • Gifts to descendants: deeds from a parent to a child or grandchild avoid the state levy.
  • Lender foreclosure: transfers made through foreclosure or in place of it, though a resale afterward is taxed.
  • Land contracts: exempt until legal title passes.

A seller who overpaid on an exempt transfer may request a refund from the Department of Treasury.

sections.h2: Papers a house sale puts on record
sections.html:
A typical sale records a deed and, where a mortgage existed, a discharge. Each is filed separately with its own fee.

  • Deed: warranty, quitclaim or personal representative form.
  • Mortgage discharge or assignment: $30, plus $3 for every extra instrument it covers.
  • Tax foreclosure papers: forfeiture and redemption certificates, notices of judgment and auction deeds. Their fees may be settled within 30 days after the sale or transfer.
  • Transfer affidavit: kept with the local assessor, which in Flint is the city Assessments Division, so it never reaches the register.

Ask the office what it accepts for each paper, including whether it takes the paper electronically.

sections.h2: What a tax foreclosure judgment does to recorded title
sections.html:
For an owner who lost a house to tax foreclosure, or a buyer thinking about a former tax parcel, the recorded judgment is the paper that matters. It clears most of what is on the books. When the judgment takes effect on March 31, title vests in the foreclosing unit, which in Genesee is the county treasurer, and liens and interests on the parcel are extinguished. Some things survive: future installments of special assessments, environmental liens filed by government agencies, severed or leased oil and gas interests, visible or recorded easements and private deed restrictions.

The paper trail lands at the register's desk. A notice of judgment goes on record, and later so does the deed from an auction. Redemption stays open through March 31. After that date the former owner has no claim, and the buyer at the county auction relies on the recorded deed.

sections.h2: Old land descriptions and your title
sections.html:
If a deed in your chain uses an older description, or cites a township that was later renamed or split, tell the title company early so any correction deed can be recorded before the sale closes. Genesee County's land history goes back to the 1830s, which is why old deeds can describe parcels by township surveys that no longer match current boundaries.

Many sellers assume the register will catch a mistake at the counter. It won't, because staff index what is handed to them and the person who prepared the deed answers for its contents. A misspelled grantor name or a mortgage discharge nobody filed also has to be fixed before a closing can finish. Ask the title company to read the recorded chain well before the closing date, not on the last day.

sections.h2: Where the other property records sit
sections.html:
Four offices hold the records a seller is likely to need, and only the register holds the recorded documents.

  • Register of Deeds, Suite 1A: deeds, mortgages, discharges, liens and foreclosure notices.
  • Equalization, Suite 8B: parcel descriptions and land records for every municipality except Flint, with assessment data left to the local assessor.
  • Flint Assessments Division: Flint's own parcel records, transfer affidavits, splits and combinations.
  • County Treasurer, Suite 2A: payoffs on delinquent tax and foreclosure information.

Before closing, order a payoff from the treasurer if tax is overdue, and confirm with the assessor that the parcel description matches the deed.

sections.h2: Why the record matters to a seller
sections.html:
Title companies and buyers read it as the public chain of ownership. Genesee has 185,007 housing units and 167,334 households, with owners in 70.7% of homes. A seller with a house that needs work or carries back tax can sell as-is for cash, and the payoff comes out of the proceeds when the deed is recorded.

A short checklist before listing:

  1. Pull your recorded deed and confirm the name and description match your ID and survey.
  2. Check that every old mortgage has a recorded discharge.
  3. Ask the treasurer for a payoff if any tax is overdue.
  4. Bring the deed, the fee and any value affidavit to the closing agent.

faqs.q: What does the register charge to file a deed in Genesee County?
faqs.a: The state's baseline in MCL 600.2567 is $30 per document of any length. Because charter counties can set their own amounts, confirm the current Genesee County figure with the office before you pay.

faqs.q: Where do I find the Genesee County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is in the County Administration Building, 324 S Saginaw St, Suite 1A, Flint, MI 48502. It is open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00, excluding holidays.

faqs.q: Is a recorded deed automatically valid?
faqs.a: No. Recording makes a document public and does not make it legal. The deed still needs proper signatures, a correct description and a grantor who owns the land.

faqs.q: Who writes the transfer tax check when a Genesee County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller does, to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed changes hands. The two levies are $3.75 and 55 cents on each $500 block of price.

faqs.q: Do I owe transfer tax on a deed to my child?
faqs.a: A deed to a child, stepchild, adopted child, grandchild or step-grandchild escapes the state tax. The deed is still recorded, and the usual filing fee applies.
